body: Prefix reuse improves LLM inference by sharing the KV cache of common prompt prefixes. This helps only if the scheduler can execute a matched branch in the current worker round. Schedulers assume that a matched prefix is ready, which holds for full attention but fails for hybrid LLMs. There, a branch (the consumer) may need recurrent state that another branch (the producer) is still computing in the same round. The native scheduler stops its waiting-queue scan at this blocked consumer, and the resulting head-of-line blocking creates execution bubbles: idle batch slots that independent work could fill. We introduce RadixFlow, which decouples prefix matching from state readiness. Its state-ready traversal turns a global scan barrier into a local wait: only the consumer is blocked until the next round, while feasible independent branches keep filling the batch under the native state check. On five hybrid models, RadixFlow lowers mean latency by 3% to 24% and worker rounds by 11% to 44% at almost unchanged reuse. On the larger Qwen3.5 models, ablations show that most of the gain comes from traversal, which adds little on a full-attention control. Heavier rounds limit how much of this saving reaches latency.
summaryZh: RadixFlow 提出了一种针对混合大模型（Hybrid LLMs）推理的调度优化方案。通过解耦前缀匹配与状态就绪性，该方法避免了因消费者分支等待生产者分支计算而导致的头阻塞（Head-of-line blocking）现象，从而消除了执行气泡。实验表明，该方法在多种混合模型上显著降低了延迟并提高了吞吐量。
